Growth & demand: Growth in the first half of the year was even stronger at 8.0%, and the Economic Survey projects real GDP growth of 6.8% to 7 .2% for FY2026-27 , while assessing that India's medium- term potential growth has risen to around 7%.

On the demand side, private consumption grew 7 .0%, lifting its share of GDP to 61.5%, the highest since FY12, aided by GST rate rationalisation and income tax relief, while fixed investment grew 7 .8%, taking the investment rate to 30% of GDP.

In volume terms, consumption stood at 10.8 millions tonnes in CY2024 and is projected to rise to 13.8 millions tonnes by CY2030, with realisation growth expected to outpace volumes as input costs, tighter regulatory standards and the shift toward more complex, eco-friendly formulations add to pricing.
Margins & costs: Pricing offered little support for most of the year, as Technicals realisations showed no sustainable recovery until February 2026, and the increases visible from March onwards have been driven by rising input costs, a consequence of the West Asia crisis and the movement in base raw materials.
Profitability and the Balance Sheet In a dynamic year, full-year EBITDA margins improved to 9% from 8%, and PAT margins to 5% from 4%.
